Header.CaseTitle: Heritage Brewing Company Ltd v Traditional Ales Holdings Plc

Counsel.Lead: James Taylor KC; Robert Mitchell (instructed by Hogan Lovells LLP)

SummaryOfPosition.Summary: The Appellant seeks a declaration of invalidity of the Respondent's trade mark registration on grounds of bad faith, prior use and likelihood of confusion with the Appellant's established unregistered mark.

FactsReliedOn.item: The Appellant has used the mark 'HERITAGE ALE' since 2008 for craft beers sold in the Cotswolds region.
The Respondent registered 'HERITAGE ALES' as a trade mark in 2020.
The Appellant has built substantial goodwill through farmers' markets, local pubs and regional festivals.
The Respondent's directors were aware of the Appellant's use when applying to register.
Since registration, the Respondent has demanded the Appellant cease use of its established mark.

Contentions.item: The registration was made in bad faith with knowledge of the Appellant's prior use.
The marks are confusingly similar for identical goods.
The Appellant has established goodwill in the 'Heritage Ale' name.
Use of the registered mark would constitute passing off.
